A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DTS research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched across the extensive reformatting and table relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original DTS experiments on visual classification, language understanding and generation, including unseen-task evaluations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds reconstruction-timing results, expanded component ablations and a K-means thresholding comparison.

M1.justification: Main-text Eq. (6) changes scaling from L2-norm ratios, producing root-mean-square magnitudes, to L1-norm ratios, producing arithmetic means. The overall DTS framework remains. However, appendix Eq. (12) retains L2 scaling, leaving the procedure used for the reported results unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the eight visual datasets, 30-task visual suite, GLUE tasks, MMLU/TruthfulQA/BBQ and the same held-out tasks. Experiments without access to pretrained weights already appear in v1 Section 9.5; their appearance in v2 is not new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds rank-1 LoRA as an evaluated comparator for accuracy and task-switching time on ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14 and Qwen-14B. Comparator membership in the matched original benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces switching-time measurement in milliseconds and expands component-ablation configurations to include r = 0.08 alongside r = 0.3 (Tables 8–9). Existing benchmark splits, backbones and metrics are retained. The newly documented rank-selection formula does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds median-versus-K-means thresholding analysis on seen and unseen tasks (Table 14), expands decomposition and low-storage ablations (Table 8), and examines reconstruction efficiency (Table 9). The original sparsity, similar-task and difference-vector analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Most matched numerical results are identical. Table 1 changes FREE-Merging's SUN397 score from 77.10 to 74.00 and Cars from 78.23 to 77.23, while retaining the average 89.74. v2 also adds ablation, timing and K-means results; for example, K-means yields unseen-task averages of 55.76 for DTS-T and 55.37 for DTS-D.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 adds an Eckart–Young–Mirsky justification for truncated SVD and a groupwise mean-squared quantization-error argument supporting arithmetic-mean scaling. Appendix Section 8.1 additionally derives a bit-budget inequality and closed-form rank rule, Eqs. (17)–(18), absent from v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the performance-degradation criticism to basic merging methods and explicitly credit prior personalized methods with preserving performance, sharpening DTS's storage-efficiency positioning. The central DTS variants, approximately 1% storage claim and unseen-task generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of difference vectors as residuals around shared knowledge and explains deployment efficiency through offline embeddings and cached reconstructed weights. Section 9.2 also qualifies K-means thresholding gains as non-universal on unseen tasks.

D1.justification: v2 documents a layerwise rank-selection formula, identifies CLIP text encoding for offline task embeddings, and specifies reconstruction once per task switch with subsequent weight caching. Its main-text storage description changes from three masks per singular-vector matrix to two bits per element, while the appendix retains six masks overall. The code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Eckart and Young citation and removes several references, including LOT Merging, core-space low-rank merging and RobustMerge. It more explicitly positions DTS against personalized methods' storage costs, while retaining the basic/personalized taxonomy and most related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the opening motivation and portions of the method explanation, condenses basic-merging related work, and revises authors, affiliations and acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and much of the experimental and appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. ViT-L/14 results move into the main text, comparison tables gain a Per column, and three tables are added, including a consolidated and expanded ablation display. The four original figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The added timing and thresholding studies provide useful evidence, and rank-selection details expand documentation. However, v2 introduces unreconciled main-text L1/two-bit versus appendix L2/six-mask descriptions. Its revised FREE-Merging row also retains an average of 89.74 although the new cells average about 89.23. These benefits and central reproducibility and numerical problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
